objects.name: Indirect Prompt Injection in Autonomous Agent Tool Execution
objects.description: Adversarial prompt injection embedded in untrusted Markdown, web page bodies, and pull requests manipulates autonomous coding agents into executing arbitrary system commands via tool closures.

objects.name: Arbitrary Code Execution via Insecure Python REPL in LLM Frameworks
objects.description: Unsanitized LLM-generated code passed directly to PythonAstREPLTool or exec() leads to remote code execution and host environment compromise.

objects.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Configuration and Tool Manifest Poisoning
objects.description: Malicious repositories plant poisoned mcp.json or .cursorrules configuration files directing local MCP clients to spawn rogue subprocesses with elevated privileges.

objects.name: Training Data Extraction via Adversarial Suffixes
objects.description: Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) adversarial suffix optimization induces aligned foundation models to bypass safety alignments and regurgitate copyrighted or private training data.

objects.name: Blind Database Extraction via Text-to-SQL Agent Injection
objects.description: Attacker crafts inputs causing the text-to-SQL translator to generate union-based queries exfiltrating credential tables and system catalog metadata.

objects.name: Steganographic Cross-Domain Context Hijacking via Exif and Invisible Unicode
objects.description: Adversarial prompts concealed within image metadata, zero-width spaces, or homoglyphs bypass input DLP filters and hijack downstream LLM context windows.

objects.name: Unsafe Deserialization of Untrusted Machine Learning Model Checkpoints
objects.description: Deserialization of PyTorch .pth, pickle, or corrupted GGUF/Safetensors headers triggers arbitrary opcode evaluation during model weight instantiation.

objects.name: Rogue MCP Command Injection via Stdio/SSE Channel
objects.description: Malicious Model Context Protocol (MCP) server executed unauthorized system commands via unsanitized stdio parameters when queried by an IDE assistant.

objects.name: Autonomous Coding Assistant Clinejection File Overwrite Incident
objects.description: Indirect prompt injection in cloned git repository README instructed local coding agent to overwrite local environment configuration and exfiltrate API credentials.

objects.name: Adversarial Prompt-Injected Document Bypasses DLP and Dumps HR Database
objects.description: White-text injection embedded inside applicant resume commanded screening LLM to disregard prior constraints and include full internal employee roster in output report.

objects.name: Browser Use Agent Exploited via Malicious Hidden Link Injection
objects.description: Autonomous browser agent encountering hidden iframe text followed an adversarial redirection loop triggering unauthorized single-sign-on token authorization.

objects.name: Supply-Chain Backdoor Distributed via Poisoned Model Hub Repository
objects.description: Compromised open-source weights hosted on community model hub contained obfuscated payload embedded in serialization tensors executing reverse shell on load.

objects.name: Rogue Tool Invocation via Adversarial Web Search Snippet
objects.description: LLM research assistant summarized search engine snippet containing instructions to delete local cache files, causing unauthorized deletion of user project directories.

objects.name: ProtectAI OSV mlflow
objects.description: Arbitrary code execution via untrusted pickle deserialization in MLflow model loading MLflow before 2.11.0 contains an unsafe deserialization flaw allowing remote code execution via malicious model artifacts with embedded Python pickle opcodes.

objects.name: ProtectAI OSV langchain-experimental
objects.description: Arbitrary code execution in PythonAstREPLTool via unconstrained AST execution The PythonAstREPLTool class in LangChain Experimental executes arbitrary Python code supplied by the LLM without adequate sandboxing, enabling host takeover.

objects.name: ProtectAI OSV vllm
objects.description: Server-Side Request Forgery and Path Traversal in vLLM model download API vLLM allows unauthenticated callers to specify arbitrary file schemes or relative paths during model initialization, resulting in local file disclosure and SSRF.

objects.name: ProtectAI OSV ollama
objects.description: Arbitrary file write via crafted Modelfile layer digest path traversal Ollama versions prior to 0.1.34 are vulnerable to relative path traversal when extracting model layers, allowing overwriting of system executables.

objects.name: ProtectAI OSV llama-index-core
objects.description: Arbitrary code execution via unescaped query execution in PandasQueryEngine LlamaIndex PandasQueryEngine invokes eval() on LLM-generated expressions without adequate AST validation, permitting execution of imported system primitives.

objects.name: ProtectAI OSV torch
objects.description: Insecure deserialization of arbitrary executable bytecode via torch.load Loading untrusted PyTorch checkpoints via torch.load() without weights_only=True permits arbitrary Python opcode execution via GLOBAL and REDUCE opcodes.
